page: Amazon Web Services m6a.48xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-based cloud instance powered by third-generation AMD EPYC 7R13 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this server provides 192 vCPUs across 96 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at a clock speed of 3.6 GHz. Memory capacity totals 768.0 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not bundle local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes, nor does it include dedicated GPU accelerators.

Hardware benchmark testing indicates exceptional high-concurrency throughput. The m6a.48xlarge achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core execution (286,813.92) and PassMark CPU metrics, including encryption, physics, and extended instruction benchmarks. Synthetic in-memory performance is similarly strong, delivering 175.75 million Redis SET operations per second and cached read bandwidth reaching 12,131.63 GB/sec. Large block uncached memory throughput remains within the top 25% at 266.13 GB/sec for reads and 128.31 GB/sec for writes. Single-core tests such as Geekbench (1,666.0) and single-threaded gzip compression register within median industry thresholds.

Network infrastructure features a baseline throughput of 50 Gbps, enabling efficient handling of data-intensive workloads despite the absence of local disks. While single-threaded instruction speed reflects standard AMD EPYC architectural baselines, the massive thread count provides high compute density. The platform lacks AVX-512 extensions and bundled public IPv4 addresses, representing a deliberate trade-off favoring high-density parallel operations over vector-heavy instruction sets.

This server is well suited for large-scale enterprise applications, high-concurrency database deployments, in-memory caching clusters, Clang build farms, and distributed web serving tiers requiring significant multi-threaded throughput and sustained memory capacity.
